title: Indigenous Botanical Phytopharmacology and Endemic Flora of the Ethiopian Highlands
institutions: Aklilu Lemma Institute of Pathobiology (ALIPB), Addis Ababa University

pioneering_discoveries.mechanism_of_action: Crushed dry berries release triterpenoid saponins that act as a lethal molluscicide against Bulinus and Biomphalaria snail vectors transmitting Schistosoma mansoni (bilharzia/schistosomiasis) at concentrations below 20 ppm.
pioneering_discoveries.ecological_safety: Rapidly biodegrades within 48 hours in freshwater streams, leaving non-toxic organic residues unlike synthetic niclosamide.
pioneering_discoveries.indigenous_cultural_origin: Centuries of traditional use by Ethiopian women as natural soap for laundering cotton shawls (Netela and Gabi) in riverbanks.

pioneering_discoveries.habitat: Afromontane canopy forests between 2,400m and 3,200m altitude
pioneering_discoveries.traditional_application: Powerful anthelmintic vermifuge used across centuries for eradicating Taenia saginata (tapeworm) contracted from cultural raw beef consumption (Kifto and Tire Siga).

nutritional_architecture.drought_resilience_factor: Deep root system stores up to 200 liters of intracellular water per plant, allowing multi-year subterranean survival during severe drought cycles.

pioneering_discoveries.demographic_impact: Sustains over 20 million rural citizens in the Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples' Region (SNNPR) and Sidama.
